nodes.description: Apply SHA-256 algorithm to input data via hashlib.sha256(data).digest()

nodes.label: Write 32-Byte Hash to Output
nodes.description: Store the resulting 32-byte SHA256 digest in evm.output

nodes.label: SHA256 Execution Complete
nodes.description: SHA256 hash result available in output

ambiguities.text: The precompile address (0x02) is not explicitly stated in this module documentation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard Ethereum precompile address 0x02 for SHA256 as defined in the Yellow Paper.

ambiguities.text: The exact values of GAS_SHA256 (base cost) and GAS_SHA256_WORD (per-word cost) are not specified in this module.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume Yellow Paper values: GAS_SHA256 = 60, GAS_SHA256_WORD = 12.

ambiguities.text: Behavior for empty input (0 bytes) is not explicitly documented.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume SHA256 of empty input returns the standard SHA256 empty hash: 0xe3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

implicit_assumptions.description: The underlying hashlib.sha256 implementation is cryptographically correct and matches the SHA-256 specification (FIPS 180-4).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect hash implementation could break integrity checks, signatures, and any protocol relying on SHA256.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot find SHA256 collisions in practical time, making it safe for commitment schemes.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Collision attacks could allow commitment manipulation, signature forgery in schemes using SHA256.

implicit_assumptions.description: SHA256 computation time is linear in input size with no pathological inputs that cause excessive computation.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Pathological inputs could cause DoS by consuming more computation than gas charges account for.

implicit_assumptions.description: The gas formula (base + per-word) accurately reflects the actual computational cost of SHA256.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Underpriced gas could enable DoS attacks; overpriced gas could make SHA256 usage economically infeasible.
